headline: EL TIGRE GOES NORTH: Silver Tiger Drills 7.72 kg/t AgEq in NEW Caleigh Vein Discovery as Sonora Mine Takes Shape
snippet: Silver Tiger Metals (TSX: SLVR) released September 11 results from the Northern Area of its El Tigre Project in Sonora, Mexico, intersecting the newly discovered Caleigh Vein with drill hole ET-24-649 returning 2.1 metres at 7,715 g/t silver equivalent, including a core interval of 0.53 metres at 29,620 g/t AgEq. The Northern Area program also confirmed the Protectora Vein and a newly discovered Northern Stockwork Zone — multiple high-grade epithermal systems extending the deposit well beyond the current mine footprint. Concurrently, high-grade confirmatory assays from inside the El Tigre heap leach mine under construction validate the grade model used for mine design, while the new Caleigh discovery adds high-grade resource upside entirely outside the planned mine area. At current silver prices (~$64/oz), 29,620 g/t translates to roughly 952 oz/ton silver — confirming El Tigre as one of the highest-grade silver-gold epithermal systems in active development in Mexico.

headline: HONEYMOON RESET COMPLETE: Boss Energy Releases Updated 9-Year LOM Plan for 13.8Mlbs U3O8 as Stock Recovers From 14% Rout
snippet: Boss Energy (ASX: BOE) released a new feasibility study and economic life-of-mine plan for its Honeymoon uranium project in South Australia on September 11, confirming forecast life-of-mine production of 13.8 million pounds U3O8 over a nine-year operating period using an optimised wide-spaced five-spot wellfield design for in-situ recovery. The study replaces a prior version Boss withdrew due to 'faulty production assumptions' and incorporates two years of real operating data since production restarted in April 2024. FY2027 guidance is set at 1.25–1.30 million pounds U3O8 as Honeymoon transitions from old to new wellfield spacing in what the company calls a 'transition year.' Resources stand at 20.8 million pounds U3O8 at 100 ppm cut-off (13.7 Mlbs Indicated, 7.1 Mlbs Inferred). BOE shares recovered after a sharp 14% fall on the earlier H2 2026 update, with the new LOM providing a cleaner framework at spot uranium near US$90/lb.

headline: FED HIKE ODDS HIT 90%: Gold Holds $4,385 Anyway as CPI Day Proves Metals Aren't Just a Rate-Hike Trade
snippet: The August CPI print — 0.4% monthly, 3.4% year-over-year released September 11 — pushed Federal Reserve rate-hike odds to 90% on CME FedWatch, yet gold ended the session holding above $4,385 and silver fell just 2.6% to $64.90, with the gold/silver ratio widening to 67.6. GoldSilver.com's analysis argues the resilient gold price signals a key insight heading into next week's FOMC meeting: at 90% implied odds, the hike is already in the price, and the real asymmetric trade is positioning for the post-decision relief rally. The metal typically weakens into an anticipated hike cycle, then firms once the event is behind it — and with futures positioning still crowded at approximately 228,000 net managed-money longs, the range-bound move on a hot CPI print suggests much of the bad news is priced.

headline: DON'T TRADE THE FED: Money Metals Makes the Case That Hiking Rates Can't Break the Gold Bull — History Backs Them Up
snippet: Writing ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC decision, Money Metals Exchange argues that precious metals investors are systematically overweighting the Fed's hike-or-hold binary. The author — leaning slightly toward a hike, but calling it roughly 50-50 — makes the historical case that 'a rate hike isn't bearish for gold and silver, as conventional wisdom would have you believe,' pointing to prior tightening cycles where gold firmed once terminal rate anxiety cleared. With gold's structural drivers — central bank demand, dollar reserve share erosion, sovereign debt dynamics, de-dollarization — operating independently of short-term Fed policy, investors who sell into the FOMC meeting may be exiting at exactly the wrong moment. A useful contrarian counterweight to the dominant market narrative ahead of next week's binary catalyst.

headline: THIRD WEEKLY LOSS, POSITIONING SPLIT: How the Market Is Lining Up Ahead of the September 15-16 Fed Decision
snippet: Precious metals ended their third consecutive losing week as the September 11 CPI print cemented market expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next week. GoldSilver.com's positioning analysis identifies a significant split in trader behaviour: one cohort is cutting longs defensively ahead of the rate decision while another is adding to existing positions on the thesis that the hike is already priced and the post-FOMC relief trade is the bigger opportunity. The divergence creates asymmetric conditions: if the Fed hikes with dovish language, a short-squeeze could amplify any move higher; if the Fed signals further tightening, crowded longs at approximately 228,000 net managed-money contracts face a flush toward the $4,050–$4,100 support zone. Both camps are positioning ahead of one of the most binary precious metals events of the year.

headline: ONTARIO SILVER MONSTER KEEPS GOING: Nord Precious Metals Drills 20,675 g/t Ag + Cobalt at Castle East Robinson Zone
snippet: Nord Precious Metals (OTC: NPMMF) reported September 9 assay results from wedge hole CS-26-140W1 at its Castle East high-grade silver project near Gowganda, Ontario, returning 20,676 g/t silver (603 oz/ton Ag) with 1.16% cobalt over 0.30 metres and a second interval of 10,413 g/t silver over 0.30 metres in the same hole. The results continue the Robinson Zone's pattern of ultra-high-grade hits at Castle East — a classic Gowganda-style silver-cobalt vein system adjacent to First Cobalt's historic mining camp. The cobalt credit adds a critical minerals dimension: cobalt is predominantly sourced from the DRC, where government export restrictions have driven prices sharply higher. Systematic wedge drilling continues to grow the Robinson Zone, with consistent ultra-high-grade intersections pointing toward a cohesive and expanding high-grade silver-cobalt corridor.

headline: JIANXIAWO STAYS DARK: CATL's Lithium Flagship Loses Environmental Licence, Benchmark Slashes 2026 Output Forecast 49%
snippet: China's Jianxiawo lepidolite mine — CATL's flagship lithium operation and responsible for approximately 4% of global lithium supply — has had its Environmental Impact Assessment revoked by Chinese regulators and is back in care and maintenance, after CATL briefly attempted to quietly resume mining in July while a tailings pond dispute remained unresolved. Over 70 complaints filed with regulators triggered swift enforcement action. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence has cut its 2026 mined output forecast for Jianxiawo from 62,500 to 32,000 tonnes of LCE — a 49% reduction — while the 2027 forecast remains unchanged at ~99,000 tonnes, pending satisfactory resolution of an environmental review that could stretch into Q4 or 2027. For the lithium market, Jianxiawo's shutdown is the most significant supply disruption of the year, creating a paradoxical squeeze where Chinese domestic supply tightens even as global lithium carbonate prices have been pressured lower by Australian mine restarts.

headline: MINING OWNS THE TSX: Record 60% of 2026 TSX30 Goes to Mining — 11 of 18 Are Former TSXV Grads
snippet: The Toronto Stock Exchange's 2026 TSX30 — announced September 9 — features 18 mining companies claiming a record 60% of the 30 spots. Montage Gold Corp. (TSX: MAU) ranked second overall with a 2,502% three-year dividend-adjusted gain, followed by Faraday Copper (TSX: FDY) at 688%, Aclara Resources (TSX: ARA) at 587%, and Trilogy Metals (TSX: TMQ) at 570%. The most significant signal for junior mining investors: 11 of the 18 mining winners graduated from the TSX Venture Exchange, confirming the TSXV-to-TSX transition as the primary value-creation pathway in the current cycle. The commodity mix has diversified beyond gold and silver for the first time in meaningful numbers — copper, rare earth and critical mineral developers also landed on the list — a structural indicator that capital is following the energy transition as much as the traditional safe-haven thesis.

headline: SPAIN EYES ITS NEW YORK GOLD: Central Bank Faces Growing Pressure to Join Europe's Repatriation Wave
snippet: Spain's 281-tonne, €33-billion gold reserve includes an undisclosed portion sitting in the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's vault — an arrangement the Banco de España has maintained under Cold War-era confidentiality agreements, with no public figure given for the NY holding. As the Netherlands (86 tonnes recently repatriated from North America to London) and France proceed with partial repatriation, Spanish voices are now asking why Madrid has not followed. The geopolitical backdrop — U.S. tariff disputes, dollar weaponization concerns, and a broader sovereign de-dollarization trend — has elevated the political sensitivity of cross-border gold holdings. For gold investors, central bank repatriation matters structurally: each repatriation event requires physical gold allocation and delivery rather than paper settlement, tightening the available float and adding a durable bid to spot prices that operates independently of speculative futures positioning and FOMC cycle dynamics.
